title: Late Breaking Results: Routability-Driven FPGA Macro Placement Considering Complex Cascade Shape and Region Constraints
problem: FPGA macro placement must satisfy cascade shape and region constraints while reserving space for cell placement and ensuring routability. This placement stage substantially influences the feasibility and quality of subsequent cell placement and routing.
motivation: Effective macro placement is critical in FPGA physical design as it directly determines the success of downstream placement and routing stages.
method: A hierarchical placement approach combining: (1) routability-driven mixed-size analytical global placement that distributes macros and cells while respecting cascade shape and region constraints; (2) integer linear programming-based cascade shape legalization to remove constraint violations; (3) matching-based macro legalization to eliminate overlaps while maintaining region constraints; (4) routability-driven detailed macro placement refinement.
key_novelty: Integration of cascade shape and region constraints within a unified routability-driven hierarchical placement framework combining global, legalization, and detailed stages.
contributions: Routability-driven mixed-size analytical global placement considering cascade shape and region constraints
Matching-based macro legalization for overlap removal with region constraint satisfaction
primary_theme: FPGA macro placement with routability constraints
